extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: C-EVAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite comprising 13,948 multiple-choice questions across 52 diverse disciplines, ranging from humanities to science and engineering. The questions span four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. C-EVAL is designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The primary source of data is mock exams freely available on the internet. A portion of college-level questions are past exam questions from top universities in China, publicly shared by students. A minor fraction of college questions are mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam, sourced from the Weipu website.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams from the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website. Data came primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All questions are processed to include exactly four choices. Questions with fewer than four options are eliminated, and incorrect choices are randomly dropped for questions with more than four options.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents are initially processed into text. All questions are parsed – automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors – into a structured format. For subjects with complex mathematical notations, questions are manually converted into standard LaTeX formats. All questions go through standard data preprocessing pipeline, such as deduplication and cleaning. Questions undergo several rounds of human validation by the authors, and all LaTeX notations are ensured to be compiled without syntax errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Explanation data for the development split is generated by combining automatic generation and human annotation. GPT-4 is prompted to generate step-by-step explanations for the ground-truth answers, then the generated explanations are manually revised to obtain the final explanations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Explanation data generation combines automatic generation and human annotation to produce high-quality explanation data for the development split. Specifically, GPT-4 is first prompted to generate step-by-step explanations for the ground-truth answers, then the generated explanations are manually revised by the authors to obtain the final explanations.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question has four choices and only one choice is the correct answer. For the development split, five exemplars per subject are annotated with explanations to enable few-shot chain-of-thought settings.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Ground-truth labels of the development and validation splits are released, while labels of the test split are kept private. Users submit model predictions to https://cevalbenchmark.com to obtain test accuracy, where a public leaderboard is maintained.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: C-EVAL is designed to help analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models, and foster their development and growth for Chinese users. LLMs intended for use in a Chinese environment should be evaluated on their knowledge of Chinese users' primary interests, such as Chinese culture, history, and laws.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: English benchmarks tend to exhibit geographical biases towards the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them. C-EVAL is designed to evaluate LLMs on knowledge of Chinese users' primary interests, such as Chinese culture, history, and laws, as well as other competencies unique in Chinese society.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: C-EVAL is designed for testing and validation of foundation models' advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities in a Chinese context. The dataset can be used to assess LLMs across multiple dimensions and analyze important strengths and limitations. Subsets can be separately utilized to assess certain model abilities of interest.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The primary source of our data is mock exams freely available on the internet. In addition, a portion of the college-level questions are past exam questions from top universities in China, publicly shared by the students. A minor fraction of college questions are mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam, sourced from the Weipu website – these questions are not freely available to the public, and we have obtained their authorization to include around 2000 such questions into C-EVAL.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The primary source of our data is mock exams freely available on the internet. In addition, a portion of the college-level questions are past exam questions from top universities in China, publicly shared by the students. The collected data come in various formats, primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages. All questions are subsequently parsed – automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors – into a structured format.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The primary source of our data is mock exams freely available on the internet. In addition, a portion of the college-level questions are past exam questions from top universities in China, publicly shared by the students. A minor fraction of college questions are mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam, sourced from the Weipu website. The collected data come in various formats, primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: All the questions in C-EVAL are processed to include exactly four choices. Most of the original questions were accompanied by four choices already, and we eliminate questions with fewer than four options and randomly drop incorrect choices for questions with more than four options.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: PDF documents are initially processed into text. All questions are subsequently parsed – automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors – into a structured format. For subjects with complex mathematical notations such as many subjects in the STEM category, we manually convert them into standard LATEX formats. All questions also go through the standard data preprocessing pipeline, such as deduplication and cleaning. Following this, the questions undergo several rounds of human validation by the authors, and all the LATEX notations are ensured to be complied without syntax errors.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: To facilitate the potential usage of C-EVAL in a few-shot COT setting, we combine automatic generation and human annotation to produce high-quality explanation data for the development split. Specifically, we first prompt GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanation to explain the ground-truth answer, then we manually revise the generated explanations to obtain the final explanations.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Specifically, we first prompt GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanation to explain the ground-truth answer, then we manually revise the generated explanations to obtain the final explanations.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: While ground-truth labels of the development and validation splits are released, we keep the labels of the test split private. This is to ensure the fair use of the C-EVAL, as the C-EVAL data may unconsciously be included in pretraining data due to web crawling. Instead, users are required to submit their model predictions to https://cevalbenchmark.com to automatically obtain the test accuracy, where a public leaderboard is maintained.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We anticipate C-EVAL will help analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models, and foster their development and growth for Chinese users. LLMs intended for use in a Chinese environment should be evaluated on their knowledge of Chinese users' primary interests, such as Chinese culture, history, and laws, as well as other competencies unique in Chinese society.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We also note that, C-EVAL, along with all the English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present C-EVAL, the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. In addition to its use as a whole, we envision C-EVAL as a suite of benchmarks, subsets of which could be separately utilized to assess certain model abilities of interest and analyze important strengths and limitations of foundation models.
